label: copy-phase feedback of r/y in long sequences (t>=10)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during original input or at <DEL>), when a token that already appeared is fed back in, and only from recall_idx 2 onward (input = orig(1) or later). It is driven mostly by the input token: r (~55% of mass, 14x lift) and y (~20%), with weaker firing on k, s, l, n, d. It depends strongly on absolute step and length: nearly silent for L<=6 and t<10, peaks at t=11-12 (L=9 is ~64% of mass), with a small rise again at t=16-17. The largest activations are r/y fed back as orig(1)/orig(2) in L=9 sequences. Inputs r/y at recall_idx 0-1 or in short sequences do not fire. Precision is only ~0.38: many r/y inputs at t>=10 stay inactive, apparently depending on hidden-state context that no simple predicate captures. Adding k/s raises mass recall to 0.84 but cuts precision to 0.24.
